root_cause.text: The original commit deferred hugetlb VMA lock allocation to a post-insertion success hook, but if a failure occurred after mmap_prepare and before the success hook, the lock would leak because the success path was never executed.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "The patch incorrectly handled hugetlb VMA lock allocation at the mmap_prepare stage, where a failed allocation occurring after mmap_prepare is called might result in the lock leaking." The revert removes the success hook and hide_from_rmap_until_complete, and returns lock allocation to inside `hugetlb_reserve_pages` during the normal mmap call, ensuring proper error handling.

candidates.rationale: This line allocates the hugetlb VMA lock in the success hook, deferred after VMA insertion. If a failure occurs after mmap_prepare and before this hook is called, the lock is never allocated, but more critically, if the lock was allocated earlier (elsewhere), the success path is needed to free it; here it is the sole allocation point, so any failure before this hook means the lock is not allocated, but the root cause states a leak occurs. Actually, this line is the deferred allocation; the vulnerability is that any post-prepare failure skips this allocation, but the lock should have been allocated earlier in prepare to be freed on error? Regardless, this statement implements the deferral that causes the vulnerability.

This statement registers the success hook that will allocate the VMA lock after insertion. By deferring the allocation to this hook, any failure between the end of mmap_prepare and the invocation of this hook (e.g., VMA insertion failure) prevents the lock from ever being allocated, or if the lock was allocated earlier, it leaks because the success path (which would free it) never runs. This registration is the mechanism of the deferral.

This statement hides the VMA from rmap until the success hook completes, which is part of the deferred lock allocation scheme. If a failure occurs before the success hook runs, the VMA may be left in an incomplete state, and the lock (if allocated elsewhere) may leak. This flag is integral to the problematic deferral.

This conditional ensures the success hook is only set when mmap_prepare succeeds. Once set, any later failure before the success hook causes the lock (if allocated earlier) to leak or, if allocated only in the hook, the lock is never allocated and the expected lock is missing, breaking the design. The condition is the gate for the deferral.

This function definition is the success hook that defers the VMA lock allocation. It is the core of the vulnerability because it moves allocation to after insertion, making it susceptible to failures in between that cause the lock to never be allocated or to leak if allocated earlier.
